properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 18 at 2:06AM EDT until September 23 at 4:00AM EDT by NWS Northern Indiana
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Indiana...

Wabash River near Bluffton IN affecting Wells County.

Wabash River near Linn Grove affecting Adams and Wells Counties.

...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Indiana...

Saint Marys River at St. Mary's River near Fort Wayne affecting
Allen IN County.

For the Wabash River...including Linn Grove, Bluffton IN...Moderate
flooding is forecast.
For the Saint Marys River...including St. Mary's River near Fort
Wayne...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Wabash River near Bluffton IN.

* WHEN...Until late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...At 16.0 feet, The outlying portion of West Washington
Street becomes impassible and SR 116 west of Bluffton begins to
flood.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:45 AM EDT Friday the stage was 15.4 feet and slowly falling.
- Bankfull stage is 8.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:45 AM EDT Friday was 15.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage early
Tuesday morning and continue falling to 8.9 feet Tuesday evening.
- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Detailed river forecasts and additional information can be found at
www.weather.gov/iwx under Rivers and Lakes.

This statement will be updated within the next 12 to 24 hours.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 18 at 7:52AM MDT until September 18 at 8:15AM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
At 752 AM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located near Wellington, or
9 miles southeast of Price, moving northeast at 20 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

Locations impacted include...
Wellington, Sunnyside, and East Carbon.

This includes US Route 6 between mile markers 248 and 259.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 17 at 10:30PM MDT until September 18 at 2:15PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southeastern Lincoln County in central New Mexico...
West Central Chaves County in southeastern New Mexico...

* WHEN...Until 215 PM MDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flood waters in Whitetail Canyon will flow into the Rio
Felix overnight into Friday morning. Flooding of low water
crossings along the Rio Felix are expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1026 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly
in the warned area. Between 3 and 5 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are possible in the
warned area. Impacts are expected within Whitetail Canyon, along
Picacho Road, including Clements Ranch, in and along the Rio
Felix.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Southeastern Lincoln and West Central
Chaves Counties.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.areaDesc: Citrus, FL; Levy, FL; Marion, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 18 at 9:18AM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Marion, Levy and Citrus
Counties.

.The Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon has been steadily rising since
July, and on September 15 reached flood stage. The cause of the high
water along the Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon is due to excessive
hydrilla growth (from the river bottom to the water surface) along a
4.5 mile stretch of river between US 41 and Lake Rousseau.  The
hydrilla is acting like a dam and holding water back, causing water
levels to rise.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 28.2 feet, Docks and boat ramps flood along the river
in Citrus and Marion counties.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:45 AM EDT Friday the stage was 28.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 28.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage this
afternoon and continue rising to 28.2 feet this afternoon.
Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 28.2 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.2
feet on 10/02/1979.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 1215 AM EDT.

properties.areaDesc: Gulf of America including Dry Tortugas and Rebecca Shoal Channel
properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued September 18 at 10:08AM EDT until September 18 at 11:00AM EDT by NWS Key West FL
properties.description:
SMWKEY

The National Weather Service in Key West has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Gulf of America including Dry Tortugas and Rebecca Shoal Channel...

* Until 1100 AM EDT.

* At 1008 AM EDT, a strong thunderstorm was located over Dry
Tortugas, moving north at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...National Weather Service Meteorologist.

IMPACT...Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly higher
waves, frequent lightning, and heavy downpours.

* Locations in the warning include...
Fort Jefferson, Dry Tortugas, Pulaski Shoal Light, Dry Tortugas
Light, and Tortugas Ecological Reserve North.
properties.instruction:
Prepare for wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, steep and fast-building
seas, frequent lightning, and blinding downpours. Stay low or go
below, and make sure all on board are wearing life jackets.
